articleTitle: GLR-Net:Generic Latent Representation Network for Missing Modality Brain Tumor Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The accurate segmentation of brain tumors is crucial for clinicians to diagnose conditions and plan surgeries. Convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods have made significant progress in brain tumor segmentation. However, real clinical environments often face issues with missing modalities. To address this, we propose GLR-Net, a network that uses shared representation learning for brain tumor segmentation with missing modalities. GLR-Net learns general latent representations from multi-modal features, which avoids the costs and quality issues of synthesizing missing modalities. The framework includes a multi-encoder-multi-decoder structure with unimodal branches for feature learning and a common multi-modal branch for joint segmentation. A modal correlation learner is also introduced to enhance robustness in scenarios with missing modalities. Experimental results on the BraTS 2019 and BraTS 2020 datasets validate the effectiveness of GLR-Net, which achieves robust brain tumor segmentation even with missing modalities.

articleTitle: Adaptive Tamper Detection and Self-Recovery of Medical Images Based on Image Inpainting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-recovery mechanism for tampered medical images based on image inpainting. During the watermark embedding phase, the algorithm proposes to embed the lesser watermarks in the contour edge region of the image. In the stage of recovering the tampered region, the algorithm proposes to recover the tampered region with the help of an image inpainting algorithm that transforms the tampered block matching problem into a minimization problem of non-local self-similar image blocks. Experimental results demonstrate that the average PSNR of the watermarked image is more than 50 dB for a watermark capacity of 0.015625. Additionally, when the tampering rate is below 20%, the average PSNR of the restored tampered medical image surpasses 40 dB.

articleTitle: Surgical Instrument Segmentation Network by SAM and Gradient Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The real-time segmentation of surgical instruments plays a crucial role in robot-assisted surgery. However, it is still a challenging task to implement deep learning models to do real-time segmentation for surgical instruments due to substantial expertise and time required for image labeling. The emerging Segment Anything Model (SAM) exhibits impressive capabilities in zero-shot segmentation for natural images. In this paper, we propose an Multi-Feature SAM (MFSAM), which can segment surgical instruments with few training data. MFSAM adopts encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder is the pre-trained network image encoder of SAM, and the decoder consists of gradient convolutional block and transposed convolution. The image encoder is utilized as the encoder, leveraging pre-trained knowledge to expedite convergence speed and mitigate training costs. By capturing semantic dependencies of gradient features through gradient convolutional blocks, emphasis is placed on target regions, thereby facilitating surgical instrument localization. Transposed convolution is employed for up-sampling feature maps to obtain refined edges. With fewer training samples, MFSAM achieves accurate segmentation of surgical instruments. The proposed network is evaluated on endovis 17, the results demonstrate that MFSAM achieves state-of-the-art performance. The proposed method can precise identification of corresponding surgical instruments while providing valuable auxiliary information to assist doctors in endoscopic surgery,

articleTitle: CQUPT-HDS: Health Big Data Security Monitoring Scheme for the Whole Life Cycle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Federal Learning (FL) has made remarkable achievements in the medical field, but the technology still faces challenges in data sharing and privacy protection, which limits its application in the medical field. To solve these problems, we developed the CQUPT-HDS system. The system is dedicated to solving the security and privacy protection problems in cross-domain collaborative analysis, ensuring the security of data and models. In view of the sensitivity of medical data, complexity of cross-domain sharing and privacy protection, key technologies such as local differential privacy algorithm and searchable encryption algorithm are adopted to optimize model training, data transmission and role rights management, so as to achieve secure and efficient cross-domain data sharing and collaborative computing. The purpose of introducing the system is to realize comprehensive security situation awareness and detection, build a multi-level defense system, solve the challenges of data sharing and privacy protection in the medical field, and provide a reliable solution for cross-domain sharing and collaborative computing of medical data.

articleTitle: Accurate Neuroanatomy Segmentation Based on Voxel-wise Densely Predicted Network Using Multi-task Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Deep learning-based methods have achieved great progress in brain segmentation based on magnetic resonance (MR) images. In this paper, we proposed a new neural network, and adopted 3D patches as input to train the model through multi-task learning for accurate segmentation of neuroanatomy, referred to as VoxelNAT. This network was trained to label the central voxel of all possible input 3D patches, generating densely voxel-wise segmentation for each one of testing magnetic resonance MRI images. Additionally, we employed an online full patch sampling strategy to train the VoxelNAT. Experimental results demonstrated that our method exhibited excellent performance in brain MRI image segmentation than alternative state-of-the-art methods. Our VoxelNAT holds significant potential for application in brain image segmentation.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Seismic Network-Inspired Myocardial Infarction Detection and Localization Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are one of the most significant public health issues globally, Among CVDs, myocardial infarction (MI) has a particularly high mortality rate. Early prediction of MI can reduce related complications and mortality rates. Inspired by the multi-channel seismic network, named Universitat Politecnica de Catalunya- Universidad Central de Venezuela (UPC-UCV), this study improves the moving step and order of filters of UPC-UCV to construct a MI detection model and name it UPC-UCV-MI. Meanwhile, we combine UPC-UCV with a Transformer Encoder to form a hybrid network (named MI-Hybrid) for locating the occurrence site of MI. We test the robustness of the proposed framework by using intra-patient and inter- patient experimental protocols. Under the intra-patient protocol, the average accuracies of MI detection and location have reached 99.96% and 99.67% respectively. Under the inter-patient protocol, the average accuracies of MI detection and location have reached 95.69% and 73.33%, which are better than other related models. Our models can quickly and accurately detect and locate MI, with good clinical application prospect.

articleTitle: Visual Reality based Aortic Vessel Inner Diameter Precise Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Coarctation of Aorta (CoA) is a well-known congenital heart defect (CHD). Observation of the internal structure of the aorta and measurement of its inner diameter are crucial for the diagnosis of CoA. Common techniques for imaging the aorta in the heart include computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Both are presented in the form of two-dimensional grayscale images and difficult for doctors to obtain important data such as internal diameters. Meanwhile, most existing virtual reality medical products lack linear measurements. Even if visualization of organs in virtual space is achieved, they almost fail to measure their dimensions directly. For some software dedicated to medical imaging, although the measurement function is possible, the doctors do not have a direct view of the measurement site, and it is difficult to quickly measure different parts of the same organ. The author proposes a VR system to carry out linear measurements on three-dimensional models of aortic vessel. It includes two different linear measurement methods, the Line method and the Ray method, using objects in the built Visual Reality scene. The results indicate that the proposed system provides good multi-directional observation effects and achieves accurate and efficient measurements.

articleTitle: Reunderstanding of the Classification of Syndromes in the Traditional Chinese Medicine Classic “Shang Han Lun” Based on Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Objective: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has a long history of serving the Chinese people's heslth since its birth,as one of the crystallizations of Chinese wisdom, empazsizes the balance of Yin and Yang to keep the body healthy. The classic masterpiece “Shang Han Lun” (Treatise on Cold Damage Disorders) is one of the theoretical cornerstones of TCM, establishing a classification system of syndromes based on the Three Yang and Three Yin. This study aims to reclassify the data related to the Three Yang meridians in “Shang Han Lun” using mainstream large language models, in order to achieve a modern medical consensus-based reunderstanding of the syndrome differentiation in “Shang Han Lun.” Method: According to the “Traditional Chinese Medicine Classic Level Test Guide,” the articles on the Three Yang meridians in “Shang Han Lun” are graded. Ten articles are selected from the 1–2 level categories for data processing. The mainstream large language models ChatGLM4.0 (Chinese and English versions) and ChatGPT4.0 (Chinese and English versions) are used to classify cases based on modern medical consensus. The classification results are then statistically analyzed and compared with the original three Yin and three Yang Meridian syndrome differentiation in “Shang Han Lun.” Results: 1. Among the four sets of data, the ChatGLM4.0 Chinese version is the closest to the classification of the Three Yang meridians in “Shang Han Lun,” while the ChatGLM4.0 English version has the largest discrepancy. 2. The classification results of ChatGPT4.0 in both Chinese and English versions are moderately close to the classification of the Three Yang meridians in “Shang Han Lun.” 3. Both ChatGLM4.0 Chinese version and ChatGPT4.0 in Chinese and English versions selected the same categories as TCM, namely external infection (Taiyang meridian), digestive system diseases (Yangming meridian), and others (Shaoyang meridian). However, the ChatGLM4.0 English version classification results included the category of nervous system diseases (Yangming meridian). Conclusion: Among the existing mainstream large language models, traditional Chinese medicine demonstrates a certain degree of rationality in cross-era clinical applications. However, further research is still needed for improvement.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Different Deep Learning Models Over Diverse Mammography Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In the field of computer-aided medical diagnosis, en-suring model robustness across diverse populations is essential for maintaining consistent performance and reliability. This paper examines the classification performance of several state-of-the-art image classification models, including EfficientNet_BO, Swin- Transformer, VisionTransformer, DenseNet121, ResNeXt, and Rep V gg, across multiple breast cancer datasets. We thoroughly evaluate these models to gauge their robustness against varying data distributions and demographic differences. The results of this study provide valuable insights into developing more robust and generalizable mammography diagnostic systems, ultimately enhancing diagnostic accuracy and improving healthcare out-comes. Our findings highlight both the strengths and limitations of each model, offering a solid foundation for future research and the optimization of breast cancer diagnostic tools in varied clinical settings.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Explainability of ChatGPT Prompts by Embedding Breast Cancer Self-Screening Rules into AI Responses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Addressing the global challenge of breast cancer, this research explores the fusion of generative AI and the intricacies of breast cancer risk assessment. This study seeks to bridge the technology gap between intelligent machines and clinicians by demonstrating ChatGPT's proficiency in reasoning. The methodology employs a supervised prompt-engineering approach to enforce detailed explanations for ChatGPT's recom-mendations. Synthetic use cases, generated algorithmi-cally, serve as the testing ground for the encoded rules, evaluating the model's processing prowess. Findings highlight ChatGPT's promising capacity in processing rules comparable to Expert System Shells, with a focus on natural language reasoning. The research introduces the concept of reinforcement explainability, showcasing its potential in elucidating outcomes and facilitating user-friendly interfaces for breast cancer risk assessment.

articleTitle: Accelerating Complex Disease Treatment Through Network Medicine and GenAI: A Case Study on Drug Repurposing for Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The objective of this research is to introduce a network specialized in predicting drugs that can be repurposed by investigating real-world evidence sources, such as clinical trials and biomedical literature. Specifically, it aims to generate drug combination therapies for complex diseases (e.g., cancer, Alzheimer's). We present a multilayered network medicine approach, empowered by a highly configured ChatGPT prompt engineering system, which is constructed on the fly to extract drug mentions in clinical trials. Additionally, we introduce a novel algorithm that connects real-world evidence with disease-specific signaling pathways (e.g., KEGG database). This sheds light on the repurposability of drugs if they are found to bind with one or more protein constituents of a signaling pathway. Our network medicine framework, empowered by GenAI, shows promise in identifying drug combinations with a high degree of specificity, knowing the exact signaling pathways and proteins that serve as targets. It is noteworthy that ChatGPT successfully accelerated the process of identifying drug mentions in clinical trials, though further investigations are required to determine the relationships among the drug mentions.

articleTitle: An Integrated Approach for Improved Mammography Image Classification Using EfficientNet and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In this study, a deep learning method utilizing the EfficientNet-BO model has been developed for the purpose of classifying mammography images into three categories: benign, malignant, and benign without callback. This approach is designed to address current challenges in mammography-based diagnostics, such as the limited amount of available data for training and the difficulty of distinguishing subtle lesion features in dense breast tissue. The model has been augmented with Test-Time Augmentation and an attention mechanism that jointly highlights lesion features with the masked image, thereby increasing the focus on key diagnostic regions. Experimental results on the CBIS-DDSM dataset demonstrate that the proposed model effectively overcomes the challenges associated with limited data and small features, resulting in a substantially improved classification performance over the base model with 96.5% accuracy.

articleTitle: Region-Aware Multiple Instance Learning for Whole Slide Image Classification: Dual-Layer Attention Network Inspired by Pathologists
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Computer-aided pathological diagnosis based on whole slide image (WSI) classification plays an important role in clinical practice, and it is often formulated as a weakly supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) problem. In recent years, attention-based MIL methods have yielded a promising solution for WSI classification. However, these methods usually directly generate instance-level attention scores under weak supervision signals, which often leads to inaccurate attention localization. Moreover, they fail to model the contextual relationships among patches, which are crucial for the diagnosis of WSI, given the continuum of tissue organization. To overcome these issues, we propose a region-aware dual-layer attention MIL network (RAMIL) for WSI classification. RAMIL mimics the diagnostic process of a pathologist and divides attention generation into two steps, from region refinement to instances. Specifically, the region attention module first divides the WSI into different regions based on the spatial position relationship of the patch, evaluating their importance and optimizing the instance features. Then it can generate more reasonable instance attention and aggregate instance features through the instance attention module, achieving more accurate classification and stronger model interpretability. Extensive experiments on three large public benchmarks demonstrate that RAMIL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art WSI classification methods.

articleTitle: Dual-Domain Image Reconstruction Network Integrating Residual Attention for Sparse View Computed Tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Sparse View Computed Tomography (SVCT) is a promising technology for reducing radiation dose and improving scan speed by reducing the number of required X-ray projection images. However, the limited projection data used in SVCT often results in reconstructed images with noise and artifacts. We propose a dual-domain SVCT image reconstruction network that leverages both residual attention mechanisms and convolutional networks. The network utilizes information from both the sinogram and image domains, enabling complementary information supplementation. To further enhance image restoration, we integrate a residual attention mechanism into the Swin-Transformer architecture to mitigate feature collapse. Additionally, a parallel convolutional branch is incorporated to enhance feature extraction completeness.By leveraging the remote correlation capability of attention mechanisms and the local information extraction capabilities of convolutional networks, our model effectively extracts valuable information for reconstruction. This integration of local and global information effectively guides the reconstruction process. Experiments on the NIH-AAPM dataset demonstrate that our model effectively reduces artifacts and improves the reconstruction of complex structures, outperforming other learning-based reconstruction models.

articleTitle: Ma-HGNN+: A Hypergraph Neural Network for Depth Analysis of Multimodal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The topic of data processing has experienced major advancements due to the emergence and rapid development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). As the complexity and interconnectivity of real-world data continue to expand, there is a growing interest in mining deep relationships between the nodes in complex networks. Despite the substantial efforts and promising results achieved by prior studies, there is still a need to thoroughly leverage the intricate interconnections of data at higher order, particularly in the context of correlated and multi-modal information. Therefore, we propose Ma-HGNN+, a novel multimodal hypergraph neural network designed to comprehensively analyze the datasets containing multimodal data. The Ma-HGNN+ framework leverages the advantages of similarity within modal data and the modeling of high-order data correlation in hypergraphs to enhance data analysis, explore interconnections, and predict categories for similar data. Additionally, we introduce an attention mechanism module during the training process, which effectively utilizes high-order data correlation and crucial data. Evaluations on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that Ma-HGNN+ outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Ma-HGNN+ is available at github.com/HaoWuLab-Bioinformatics/Ma-HGNN.

articleTitle: Variational Disentangled Generative Model for Individualized Treatment Effect Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Estimating individualized treatment effect (ITE) from observational data is a challenging problem due to the lack of counterfactual outcomes and the presence of selection bias. Existing ITE estimation methods, which primarily focus on disentangled representation learning, have achieved significant success in estimating treatment effects. However, precisely learning disentangled latent factors remains an open problem. In this paper, we propose a Variational Disentangled Generative Model (VDGM) based on a collaborative strategy of Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE), Generative Adversarial Net (GAN), and Mutual Information Network Estimation. VDGM infers latent factors from observed covariates by VAE, disentangling factors into three disjoint sets corresponding to the instrumental, confounding, and adjustment factors. The disentangled latent factors can then be used to balance the distribution discrepancy between treatment and control groups, thereby reducing selection bias. Furthermore, VDGM addresses information loss by preserving useful predictive information under the regularization of a mutual information estimator. It also uses mutual information estimators to maintain the independence of disentangled latent factors. Additionally, our model uses the GAN framework to generate counterfactual outcomes for ITE estimation. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets show that the proposed method outperforms the baselines in achieving low errors in ITE estimation.

articleTitle: An Antigen Design Method Based on Molecular Dynamics and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The prediction of the impact of amino acid mutations on the change in binding free energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varDelta\varDelta \boldsymbol{G})$</tex>, is critically important for both biomedical and industrial applications, particularly in improving the binding capacity between antigen and antibody. This study presents an antigen design method based on graph neural networks that integrates molecular dynamics simulations (MD) with deep learning techniques. Initially, MD simulations identify key hotspot residues essential for protein function and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varDelta\varDelta G$</tex>. Subsequently, a deep learning model predicts the effects of mutations on the binding free energy, facilitating efficient utilization of computational resources and time. This method not only accelerates the identification of crucial residues but also predicts the mutational impacts on the binding free energy. Validation of new mutations through MD confirms the predictions of the deep learning model and provides datasets for further training of the model. This approach not only enhances the potential for designing antigens with optimized stability and functionality but also sets the stage for its further refinement and broader application in biomedical research.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Digital Health with Generative AI: User Experiences and Healthcare Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAl) is revolutionizing digital health by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, predicting health risks, and reducing wait times and costs. This study adopts an inductive approach to analyze user experiences with GenAl through social media comments. We construct a conceptual framework and find that users, including physicians and patients/general users, have varying needs that need to be met using different GenAl types. Our conceptual framework also reveals the interactions among the characteristics of GenAl, users, and users' tasks. This research advances the field of Information Systems by bridging the gap between technology and user behavior in digital health. We also offer insights for future research to explore the influence of GenAl on users' behavior efficiently and how to effectively integrate GenAl tools into their clinical workflows, enhancing patient care and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Cancer Gene Selection Algorithm Based on Neighborhood Rough Sets Combined with Quantum Genetic Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Rough Set Theory (RST) is a commonly used and effective data processing tool. To extend the range of data that RST and its related theories can handle, researchers have proposed many innovative approaches based on the Pawlak model. This paper presents an efficient phased method that incorporates a quantum genetic algorithm to address the prob-lem of attribute reduction in high-dimensional data analysis and accelerate the computation process. The research method is mainly divided into three stages: first, feature importance assessment is used to classify the feature set into three categories: deterministic, chaotic, and redundant, with redundant features being eliminated; second, the quantum genetic algorithm is applied to optimize the chaotic feature set, ensuring effective partitioning while retaining dataset information; third, the core set undergoes fine-tuning to adjust the distribution of specific attributes, making it closely align with the decision distribution, thereby achieving rapid attribute reduction. To further discuss the ability of this reduction algorithm to eliminate redundant attributes, comparative experiments were conducted using four different algorithms, and speed validation was performed using five cancer gene datasets with over 10,000 dimensions. The exper-imental results show that this method not only effectively reduces computational complexity but also overcomes the limitations of rough set theory, significantly enhancing the ability to handle large datasets, and demonstrates its potential and application prospects in high-dimensional data analysis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Method for Predicting ATRX Mutation Status in Gliomas Using Multimodal MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The ATRX gene mutation status plays a pivotal role in the diagnosis and treatment planning of gliomas. The way to get the ATRX mutation status in clinical practice is through invasive and time-consuming molecular techniques. This study explores the potential of deep learning models as a non-invasive alternative for predicting ATRX mutation status using multimodal MRI. Experiments were conducted on the publicly available TCGA-GBM and TCGA-LGG datasets, comprising preprocessed MRI sequences, glioma tumor annotations, and ATRX mutation status. Trained on these datasets, deep leaning models aim to capture subtle MRI pattern differences associated with ATRX gene mutations. In this study, we first compare the prediction performances of Uniformer V2, specialized in processing videos, with other traditional deep learning models for image classification like ResNet, DenseNet, and Efficient. The experiments demonstrate that Uniformer V2 achieved the best validation AUC of 0.868, with a validation accuracy of 0.743. Then, we take Uniformer V2 as the base model and refine Uniformer V2 by augmenting it with a modal attention module, adjusting learning rate attenuation, incorporating patient age and gender information, and selecting an appropriate loss function. Implementing these strategies, the validation accuracy improves to 0.857 with an enhanced validation AUC of 0.957.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Cross-Modal Medical Image Retrieval with Ensemble Prototype Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Cross-modal hashing for Positron Emission Tomography (PET) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) data retrieval is crucial for enhancing the understanding of disease states and developing personalized treatment strategies. Supervised cross-modal hashing methods utilize labels to optimize semantic associations. However, this approach is challenging and costly in the medical imaging field due to the extensive manual annotations required. Thus, this paper introduces a pioneering unsupervised cross-modal hashing method for medical image retrieval, called UEPA. Specifically, a higher-order similarity learning mechanism is introduced to capture subtle semantics between different data points, integrating and refining neighborhood information. Additionally, an ensemble clustering method is employed to capture category relevance, ensure the stability of prototype category information, and provide self-supervised guidance for model self-training. Finally, robust hash codes are generated by fusing higher-order similarity and category attribute relevance information. Experiments conducted on two datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: AiMed: Artificial Intelligent Large Language Model for Medicine in China
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: With the continuous growth of medical information and the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, processing medical knowledge efficiently and accurately becomes more and more important. In this study, we introduce a large language model called AiMed, which is specialized in processing Chinese medical information. AiMed is designed to solve multiple tasks such as medical knowledge QA, medical literature retrieval and reading, and it is expected to play an important role in medical research. The AiMed model is developed using a multi-stage process including pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning based on human feedback, and direct preference optimization. These steps ensure high performance of the model in understanding medical terminology, analyzing complex contexts, and generating high-quality text. The codes and parameters of this study have been open-sourced and a series of experiments was conducted to verify the validity of AiMed.

articleTitle: AgentMV: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Model For Mechanical Ventilation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Mechanical ventilation is a key therapeutic tool widely used in intensive care units for patients. Currently, clinicians rely on experience and guidelines to make mechanical ventilation decisions. However, developing personalized treatment tailored to each patient is challenging due to individual patient differences, complex disease states, and variations in clinicians' experiences. In this study, a mechanical ventilation decision-making model named AgentMV is developed under a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework, which includes state space, action space, reward function, and deep reinforcement learning algorithm. The trained model can provide the decisions of ideal body weight adjusted tidal volume (Vt), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), and fraction of inspired oxygen (Fi0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) for critically ill patients. For better action selection, we have designed the Dynamic Weighted Deep Q-Network (shortly, DWDQN) algorithm and implemented it in AgentMV. We compare AgentMV with models utilizing other advanced value-based DRL algorithms. The result shows that AgentMV achieves the highest expected return (13.49) on the test set. Then we compared the differences in actions provided by clinicians, AgentMV, and other DRL models on the test set. AgentMV tends to select lower V t (3–6 mL/Kg) settings compared to clinicians and consistently selects the lowest PEEP (0–5 cmH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>0), resulting in higher survival rates for patients. In conclusion, AgentMV can provide appropriate mechanical ventilation decisions based on patients' clinical features that probably benefit critically ill patients.

articleTitle: CautionGCN: Cancer Subtype Classification by Developing Causal Multi-Head Autoencoder and Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Cancer is an aggressive and complex disease, and its heterogeneity makes it challenging to target specific therapies for different tumor types. Predicting cancer subtypes using only single-omics data is challenging because cancer occurrence and development result from the concerted action of multiple molecular mechanisms, not a singular factor. Recently, Deep Learning approaches have become a valuable tool in cancer subtype classification. However, high-dimensional multi-omics data are typically imbalanced, with an abundance of molecular features and relatively few patient samples. This imbalance makes it difficult to conduct integrated multi-omics analysis based on deep learning. In this study, CautionGCN, a model using deep neural networks based on multi-omics data, was employed to classify breast cancer subtypes. Three types of breast cancer omics data-RNAseq, DNA methylation, and copy number variation-were collected from The Cancer Genome Atlas. The proposed model comprises the following three components. First, a similarity network among the three omics samples was constructed using a similarity network fusion method. The causal Multi-Head autoencoder then extracts the causal features of the three omics data. Finally, the sample similarity network and feature matrix were input into a graph convolutional neural network for cancer subtype classification. The robustness and classification accuracy of the model can be enhanced by identifying genetic features with causal relationships. Experimental results confirmed that our model has significantly improved performance compared to other methods, and the effectiveness of multi-omics integration and causal feature selection was identified.

articleTitle: Organ-Aware Transformer for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Transformer has been successful in NLP and vision tasks, but due to its inherent limitations, its potential applications in medical image remain largely unexplored. In order to solve the problem of lack of anatomical shape edge constraint in medical image segmentation, we proposed a Joint-scale collaborative Organ-aware Transformer (JSOT) framework to simultaneously segment myocardium (Myo), left ventricle (LV) and right ventricle (RV). JSOT consists of two parts,of which the organ-aware Transformer module is used to extract the deep features of the original image and bring the interpretability of the results. At the same time, the module reduces the quadratic computation complexity of Transformer to linear by introducing an semantic map. Then, through cross-scale collaborative fusion (CSCF) of functional modules, the adjacent depth features are fused to guide the network to carry out fine segmentation.We conducted experiments on the ACDC cardiac MRI Segmentation Challenge dataset. Thetest results obtained on ACDC dataset show that the average Dice coefficients of the proposed method on Myo, LV and RV segmentation tasks are 90.17%, 96.28% and 91.66%, respectively, and the average HD coefficients of the proposed method are 2.00, 2.09 and 4.54, respectively. Tests on the Synapse dataset show that the average Dice coefficient of the method is 81.03%, especially for large organs.

articleTitle: PIRTRE-C: A Two-Stage Retrieval and Reranking Enhanced Framework for Improving Chinese Psychological Counseling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The rapid evolution of modern society and the pervasive high-stress lifestyle have led to an increasing incidence of mental health challenges. Anxiety, depression, and stress management have become prevalent issues requiring attention, highlighting the importance of psychological counseling. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in understanding and generating natural language texts, making them versatile tools in the realm of mental health. However, current LLMs often provide generic responses during psychological counseling sessions, reflecting a lack of depth in understanding and empathy. Moreover, they struggle to identify potential psychological disorders in users during interactions and to formulate professional treatment strategies. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves text generation by integrating insights from external knowledge repositories, thereby enhancing the accuracy and fidelity of generated responses. In this study, we introduce PIRTRE-C (Psychological Information Retrieval and Reranking for Enhanced Cognition), a framework designed to address these limitations. PIRTRE-C begins by retrieving pertinent knowledge from a corpus of psychology-related data. Then, a re-ranker is employed to sequence the retrieved texts based on relevance. Finally, by utilizing the acquired information through contextual assimilation, our objective is to enable LLMs to provide more empathetic and professional responses to inquiries in psychological counseling.

articleTitle: Image Semantic Information Fusion for MR Brain Tissue Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Brain tissue segmentation from modal magnetic resonance images is valuable for the diagnosis of brain disorders, especially for neonatal brain growth patterns and for tracking the progression of neurodevelopmental disorders. However, accurate segmentation of brain tissue is a challenging task due to the blurred boundaries between brain tissue regions, low contrast due to the myelin formation process, and complex anatomical relationships. We propose a novel 3D FCN network for brain tissue segmentation. Firstly, we propose a cross-modal feature fusion (CFF) module, which cleverly integrates inter-slice information and intra-slice information in the face of multi-modal information extraction and image anisotropy of MR images. Secondly, we design a new Transformer feature extraction module (rotation-Transformer, RT) based on position transformation (rotation), which can better calculate the similarity between two patches on the basis of rotation, so as to use the image semantic information in the brain structure to integrate the remote dependency information in the plane. In addition, the boundary assistant (BA) module are introduced to integrate boundary information of brain structures. Then, we apply the CFF module, the RT module, and the BA module to a 3D FCN network with two encoding streams and one decoding stream. Evaluated on the iSeg-2017 dataset (data from infant brain MR images) and the BrainWeb dataset (data from adult brain MR images). Experimental results on the iSeg-2017 dataset and the BrainWeb dataset show that the proposed method has good performance in brain tissue region segmentation of adult and infant MR images. In particular the average Dice coefficients on the iSeg-2017 and the BrainWeb testing data reach 93.36% and 96.88%, respectively,

articleTitle: HCGN: Hierarchical Convolution and Graph Network for Predicting Knee Osteoarthritis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common joint disease that severely affects the normal lives of patients. Typically, in clinical practice, the severity of KOA is evaluated by observing X-ray images of the knee joint. This approach is highly dependent on the subjective experience of the doctor and may vary among doctors. In this study, we propose a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) model that integrates structural information processing to predict KOA severity automatically based on the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system. Specifically, (1) The knee joint regions of the original X-ray images are segmented using automatic detection for subsequent model predictions; (2) We employed popular pre-trained deep CNN models to perform feature extraction, obtain their multi-scale feature maps, and construct their corresponding graph representations; (3) A graph attention network (GAT) was designed as a fine-tuning module to build a KOA prediction model. In our experiments, we tested various pretrained models combined with a GAT fine-tuning module to evaluate their performance on the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset. The results show that our proposed method significantly improves the predictive performance in multiple aspects compared to the original model. In addition, our proposed method has good decision interpretability.(https://e:ithub.comJddw2AIGROUP2CQUPTIHCGN)

articleTitle: CytoFlow: A Novel Computational Method to Construct Signal Transduction Networks at Single-Cell Resolution Based on Flow Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The signal transduction network is essential for eukaryotic cellular communication and response to environmental signals, with disruptions leading to various diseases. As our understanding of intracellular signaling expands, the demand for computational tools that can efficiently synthesize this information into comprehensive networks grows. To meet this need, we developed CytoFlow, a novel computational model designed to construct cell-type-specific signal transduction net-works by leveraging protein-protein interaction and single-cell transcriptomics data. Specifically, it models the network from receptors to transcription factors as a penalized flow network, optimized using linear programming techniques. We validated CytoFlow's superior precision against existing methods in reconstructing the yeast mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway, and demonstrated its ability to identify cell-type-specific signaling patterns in the human prefrontal cortex and peripheral blood mononuclear cells. In summary, CytoFlow offers a precise and cost-effective solution for constructing detailed signal transduction networks, advancing our capacity to understand and analyze cellular signaling processes.

articleTitle: A Model for the Prediction of Ventilator-Associated Conditions in Patients with Acute Respiratory Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Mechanical ventilation is a crucial treatment for patients with acute respiratory failure (ARF) in the intensive care unit, which can lead to ventilation-associated conditions (VAC). Therefore, the prediction of VAC occurrence in ARF patients is a significant concern. Due to the rarity of VAC occurrence in ARF patients, the imbalanced data set in the intensive care unit poses a challenge in VAC prediction. This paper proposes a model called PVAC for predicting VAC in ARF patients including a data processing algorithm called Undersampling-SMOTE algorithm containing the undersampling ratio parameter r (USMOTE(r)) and the AdaBoost classifier trained by the processed data. The USMOTE(r)) combines random undersampling and SMOTE algorithm to handle the imbalanced data. The AdaBoost classifier outperforms the other three classifiers including decision tree, random forest, and support vector machine. Results indicate that the PVAC model has an accuracy of 71.12% and a precision of 68.89%, which exhibits the most effective predictive performance compared to classical resampling methods such as ADASYN and the latest resampling method known as the UCO algorithm. The proposed PVAC model can effectively predict whether ARF patients receiving mechanical ventilation will experience VAC.

articleTitle: PP-LDG: A Medical Privacy-Preserving Labeled Data Generation Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The rapid development of deep learning has led to an increasing demand for data. However, such data are scarce in many fields and often contain private and sensitive information, such as medical images. The fact that data owners are unwilling to share these high-privacy data further exacerbates the scarcity of data. A prevalent research direction is to combine differential privacy and image generation, by which we can obtain a large amount of synthetic data with a similar distribution to the original dataset, and that synthetic dataset does not compromise the privacy of the original dataset. However, these methods cannot provide labels for the generated data, limiting the subsequent uses of the data. To solve the problem, we propose a generic privacy-preserving labeled data generation framework named PP-LDG. It is the first data publishing framework to generate labeled data while not disclosing the privacy of original data. We theoretically demonstrate that our proposed framework can provide strict privacy guarantees with differential privacy and demonstrate the effectiveness of the synthetic dataset obtained from the framework under practical privacy budgets through extensive experiments.

articleTitle: Endoscope posture calculation method for minimally invasive surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Endoscopic surgery is the most widely used minimally invasive surgical procedure. Due to its advantages of less trauma, lower infection rate, shorter hospital stay, and faster patient recovery, almost all abdominal surgeries, including intrathoracic surgery, pelvic exenteration, and abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, can be performed through endoscopic surgery. This paper studies a new method for endoscopic positioning. This method rigidly connects a small camera to the tail of the endoscope, and fixes a checkerboard calibration board with a rigid body on the outside of the human body. The rigid body has a marker ball. By calculating the position conversion relationship between the endoscope and the camera, the camera and the checkerboard calibration board, and the checkerboard calibration board and the rigid body, the position and posture of the endoscope under the optical tracking system are obtained, so as to reduce the trouble caused by light path obstruction in endoscopic surgical navigation. After experiments, the accuracy of the endoscope position acquisition is good and has certain use value.

articleTitle: Medical image super-resolution algorithm based on multi-scale feature aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Ultrasound images are vital for medical diagnostics but often suffer from information loss and blurred details due to limitations in imaging systems and sensor technologies. Many researchers have proposed super-resolution algorithms to enhance medical images. But existing super-resolution methods struggle with the uneven distribution of noise and clarity. To address this, we propose a super-resolution algorithm for medical images based on multi-scale feature aggregation Leveraging the architecture of Unet as our primary framework, our method enhances output details through multi-scale hole convolutions. Taking into consideration the characteristics of ultrasonic images, we propose a frequency domain-based module to enhances edge information while effectively denoising the image. Furthermore, to improve the quality of the output images, we introduce an image processing module grounded in global information. The module ensures clarity while considering the overarching context, thereby preserving global consistency and enhancing output quality. We experiment on three datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of our model. Additionally, significant improvements in medical image segmentation are observed, proving the practicability of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: VSSI-L1N: EEG Extended Source Imaging Based on Variation Sparsity and Nuclear-norm Regularization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Accurately reconstructing the location and extent of cortical sources is crucial for understanding brain function and disease mechanisms. Source signals inherently possess low-rank structural characteristics and the existence of noise and background human body activities has a great influence on the source imaging results. This paper presents an Electroen-cephalography (EEG) source imaging (ESI) algorithm, VSSI-LIN. The algorithm employs a combined constraint of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>-norm and nuclear norm to improve the accuracy and resolution of cortical source reconstruction. VSSI-L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1N</inf>uses the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>-norm in the spatial variation domain to promote sparsity and extract the time-domain information, employs the nuclear norm to capture the low-rank structure of the signal, adjusting and reducing the interference of human body background activities. The solution of VSSI-L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1N</inf>can be effectively derived through the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through simulation and experiments, and it is shown to have higher accuracy and better spatial resolution. The source code of VSSI-LIN is available at https://github.com/hangj-cache/VSSI-L1N.git.

articleTitle: Cycle Based Link Prediction Method for Cross-Granularity Contrast Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In the process of network evolution, interactions be-tween network nodes often extend beyond simple binary interactions to include group interactions. Examples include social networks like those found on Facebook and research collaboration networks formed through scientific partnerships. Link prediction in research collaboration networks aims to forecast collaborative relationships among scientists, thereby enhancing our understanding and opti-mizing the structure and dynamics of these networks. However, net-work data are frequently sparse, and prediction based solely on at-tributes or structural features often yields inconsistent results. In complex networks, higher-order structures often contain more comprehensive information. Capturing the cycle structure in the graph enriches the representation of nodes as well as reduces the infor-mation loss during the information transfer process, thus improving the accuracy of link prediction between nodes. Specifically, our approach utilizes the cycle to calculate its significance and reconstructs ‘fat node’ information, which replaces node representations within the original cycle. We introduce a cycle scale module to de-termine the optimal cycle size for the graph. Moreover, by constructing the clustering coefficients of the multivariate cycle, we identify node and cluster aggregations within the graph, thereby reduce the complexity of finding cycle scales. Subsequently, a graph compari-son learning model is employed to establish a mapping between the newly generated ‘fat nodes’ and link relationships. Through experi-mental validation, our method demonstrates strong link prediction performance across various real network datasets.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Linguistic Concept Rule Extraction Algorithm for Ventilator-Associated Complications in Patients with Acute Respiratory Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Ventilator-Associated Condition (VAC) describes lung damage that arises in patients undergoing mechanical ventilation. This includes newly developed or aggravated pulmonary infiltrates, bronchitis, pneumonia, and other similar conditions. This paper primarily investigates a fuzzy reasoning method for ventilator-associated complications in patients with acute respiratory failure. It presents a rule extraction algorithm based on fuzzy linguistic concepts, aiming to perform fuzzy reasoning on whether patients are likely to develop ventilator-associated conditions (VAC) based on linguistic concepts. Firstly, the importance of features is evaluated using the Out-Of-Bag (OOB) method, and the top five features with the highest importance ranking are selected as the core attributes for this study: peep, spo2, resp-rate-total, platelet, and vt-PW. Next, appropriate fuzzy membership functions are established by fitting the distribution frequencies of the core attributes. This forms the foundation of the fuzzy linguistic decision context. Then, by considering the refined relationships between fuzzy linguistic concepts based on conditional and decision attributes under different levels of confidence, personalized linguistic rules are extracted to capture individualized requirements. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through an example. This research provides a scientific basis for uncertain reasoning and decision-making with linguistic value information.

articleTitle: Ensemble Multi-Kernel Broad Learning System for Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Medical data analysis with machine learning helps improve the efficiency of disease diagnosis. Faced with complex medical data, accurate feature selection and collective intelligence can extract diverse features. Combining the kernel method with ensemble learning, a novel Ensemble Multi-Kernel Broad Learning System (EMKBLS) is proposed. The multi-kernel fusion on the feature and decision level enables BLS to get more comprehensive feature information, resulting in excellent performance in disease diagnosis. The ablation experiment shows the effectiveness of the proposed two-level multiple kernels fusion. The comparison experiment demonstrates the progressiveness of EMKBLS among kernel and ensemble methods on disease diagnosis. The proposed method contributes to promoting the development of medical intelligence.

articleTitle: Self-supervised Representation Matching Model for Treatment Effect Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Estimating treatment effects is crucial for making informed decisions in clinical domains, but it comes with significant methodological challenges, such as missing counterfactual outcomes and treatment selection bias. Matching methods utilize the nearest-neighbor technique to minimize selection bias and estimate counterfactual outcomes. It is one of the most fundamental and widely used approaches in treatment effect estimation. However, these methods frequently encounter challenges with high-dimensional data, complex variables, and violation of the positivity assumption, which can result in biased outcomes. We propose a Self-supervised Representation Matching Model which combines feature selection, representation learning, and matching into a unique framework. To eliminate the bias introduced by irrelevant variables, this model integrates grouplevel sparse penalties into the representation network. It not only achieves feature selection and network simplification but also effectively highlights important features. A self-supervised balancing objective is employed to map the original covariate space into a nonlinear, overlapping representation space, enabling effective matching even in complex scenarios that violate the positivity assumption. We compare the proposed model with baseline methods on datasets that include the widely used semi- simulated IHDP dataset, modified IHDPs, and a real-world clinical dataset. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance compared to baseline models.

articleTitle: CLGraph: A Contrastive Learning-Based Multimodal Fusion Approach for Spatial Domain Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies provide multi-modal data for exploring tissue architecture domains, cell types, intercellular communication, and their biological consequences, including high-throughput gene expression, spatial coordinates, and histological background. In spatial domain identification, spatial transcriptomics data reveal the positions and functions of cells within tissue structures. Existing spatial domain detection methods do not fully leverage the unique spatial properties of spatial transcriptomics data and the morphological features in corresponding tissue images. To integrate the complex relationships among multimodal data, this paper proposes an optimized representation model based on graph contrastive learning. It utilizes complementary information among different modalities to jointly optimize low-dimensional embeddings of gene expression profiles. The paper validates the performance of the proposed model in spatial domain identification across multiple datasets, demonstrating consistency with biological annotations. Additionally, spatially variable genes identified based on clustering results align with certain marker genes.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Graph Completion Model with Path-Specific Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) play an increasingly im-portant role in many knowledge-aware tasks. However, existing KGs are struggle with incompleteness, which motivates Knowledge graph completion (KGC), that is, predicting the lost links between entities based on observed triples. Reasoning over relation paths in incomplete KGs is popular. Nonetheless, some significant issues are still remained to be addressed, such as path noise and ambiguity of inferred relation. To address these problems, we propose a novel path augmented _Reasoning model with avoidance of Path noise and Disambiguation of inferred relation in this paper, referred to as RPD. In this model, we calculate the sum of resource allocation for each relation path to measure its reliability to avoid the inference of path noise. To address the ambiguity of an inferred relation, we introduce position embedding to denote the relation position along the path when learning path representation. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposal RPD model in the handling of KGC tasks compared to SOTAs.

articleTitle: Gene Name Recognition in Gene Pathway Figures Using Siamese Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The number of scientific papers related to biology is rapidly increasing, and with it, the number of pathway figures containing crucial biological information. However, manually annotating these figures is a time-consuming process, and current optical character recognition (OCR) methods are not effective in identifying gene names within these figures. To improve gene name recognition from pathway figures, we utilized a Siamese network that maps image segments to a library of pictures containing known gene name, like object recognition in many photo applications. We combined the triplet convolution neural network and the spatial pyramid pooling (TSPP-Net) to create a CNN triple loss function. We trained and tested the developed TSPP-Net network using 563 gene images from 45 pathway pictures, 1000 images of alphanumeric characters and gene names from HUGO and KEGG. To benchmark against major available OCR technologies, we used 20 randomly selected curated pathway genes. Additionally, we compared several models, such as VGG19, VGG16, Resnet-50 Resnet-18, Densnet-121, and Xception for the Siamese backbone network model. VGG16 achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 93%, which is much higher than the results obtained using OCR. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/MuhammadAzam636/Siamese-Network.

articleTitle: A Multi-view Clustering Ensemble via Graph Tensor Learning in Medicine Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Medical image analysis is critical for disease diagnosis and treatment. However, the complexity and diversity of medical images make effective segmentation without prior information a significant challenge. This paper proposes a Multi-view Clustering Ensemble method via Graph Tensor Learning (MCEGTL) to enhance clustering performance by integrating information from various perspectives. The multi-view learning framework consolidates comprehensive and complementary information from different views, while ensemble learning techniques further improve clustering accuracy. Specifically, a random view grouping strategy captures the interrelationships between multiple views, enabling efficient multi-stage fusion. By expanding the multi-view data into multiple view groups, a consensus bipartite graph is constructed in the early fusion stage by jointly exploring diversity at three levels. Subsequently, diverse base clusterings are obtained through fast graph partitioning of different view groups, which are further fused into a unified bipartite graph for final clustering. The base clustering is refined into approximate graph structures using a theoretical rank constraint with an adaptive weight coefficient. Additionally, the multiple refined connectivity matrices are stacked into a third-order tensor, from which higher-order similarities are extracted via graph tensor learning. This approach also facilitates the propagation of mutual information between different graph matrices. Experiments on several medical image datasets demonstrate the advantages of the proposed MCEGTL compared to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A Survival Prediction Model for Colorectal Cancer Based on Multimodal Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: As the third most common malignant tumor in the world, colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks second in the death rate of all cancers. With advancements in medical technology and the digitization of healthcare information, an increasing amount of data on cancer patients is being collected and stored, including medical images, clinical records, diagnostic results, treatment plans, and survival data. Prognostic survival prediction based on the current stage data of patients is a common task in CRC research. Previous survival prediction models primarily relied on unimodal data, which often failed to capture the correlations and complementarities between different modalities, leading to information loss and limited modeling capability. To reduce the impact of heterogeneity in various modal data on global feature information and to enhance the extraction capacity of multimodal information, this study constructs specialized encoders for different modal data and integrates them using a multi-head attention mechanism. This design aims to capture the global information of patients' multimodal data, creating a multimodal learning survival prediction model. We conducted experiments on The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) public dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed model can more effectively extract intra-modal valuable information and leverage inter-modal interactions, significantly improving the accuracy and robustness of survival predictions compared to other benchmark models, achieving higher accuracy metrics related to survival prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Skill Assessment based on Transformer with Temporal Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a crucial emergency technique that saves lives in emergencies such as cardiac arrest. The widespread dissemination of CPR skills is essential. However, current CPR skill training and evaluation largely rely on manual labor or expensive hardware equipment, making broad promotion challenging. In this paper, a two-stage CPR skills assessment framework with transformer based on visual action analysis is proposed. First, the action classification model, Video Swin Transformer, is utilized to conduct clip-level key step recognition, and indirectly obtain video-level temporal localization of key steps. Then, the localization results are optimized using three designed temporal filtering strategies. Additionally, a self-collected CPR dataset is built, and the experiments conducted on this dataset validate the superior performance of our method. The proposed approach provides an effective safeguard for the broadly dissemination of CPR skills.

articleTitle: MoCaGCN: Cancer Subtype Classification by Developing Causal Graph Structure Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The classification of cancer subtypes is a crucial step towards more personalized treatment and has important implications for understanding the biological mechanisms of cancer subtypes. Multi-omics data present challenges in cancer research due to their high-dimensional feature spaces, significant noise, and limited sample sizes. However, the scale and heterogeneity of this data makes integration and classification a non-trivial task. Models based on correlations often contain confounding and redundant features, resulting in uninterpretability and weak generalization. Therefore, we proposed a novel multi-omics classification framework named Muti-omics Causal Graph Convolutional Network incorporated with causal structure learning and graph neural networks. Furthermore, the model can improve the performance and generalization capabilities of cancer classification by considering the prior knowledge of gene-gene interactions. This study constructed a more efficient framework for cancer subtype classification based on multi-omics data, which mainly include multi-omics data preprocessing, omics causal graph network construction, and multi-omics data integration methods. Finally, we demonstrated that our model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods with fewer variables for higher accuracy on the real lung adenocarcinoma dataset from the cancer genome atlas program.

articleTitle: Predicting Mortality Risk in Heart Failure Patients: Insights from COX Regression and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: This study is based on baseline data and 2-year follow-up information from 145 heart failure patients in Guangxi, China, combined with a publicly available scientific dataset on Chinese heart failure patients. Multiple datasets of varying scales were constructed, and traditional Cox proportional hazards models, along with Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, Random Survival Forest, and Survival Support Vector Machine algorithms were employed to develop heart failure mortality risk prediction models. These models were used to identify and quantitatively evaluate both risk factors and protective factors for HF mortality. In terms of the outcome, XGBoost demonstrated superior performance on high-dimensional datasets with missing values, whereas Support Vector Machine exhibited stronger predictive capability on similarly scaled datasets without missing values. The results based on XGBoost model and evaluation based on SHAP values further confirmed that Glomerular Filtration Rate, Height and Glucose are critical predictors. For survival time analysis, the Cox models generally outperformed Random Survival Forest and Survival Support Vector Machine algorithms. The mutual validation of different modeling approaches can enhance the robustness and effectiveness of heart failure mortality risk prediction, better supporting clinical prevention and treatment decision-making.

articleTitle: Mining Underlying Structural Insights via High-Order Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Complex networks effectively model data by representing entities as nodes and interactions as edges, revealing intricate association patterns and highlighting inherent structural information. High-order multivariate interactions play a crucial role in characterizing interactions among a group of nodes, providing insights into the complex structures inherent in data. However, multivariate interactions are not always explicitly present, necessitating the utilization of binary interaction information and attribute data to effectively mine them. Message passing allows for the efficient propagation of information through the network, and helps in understanding dynamic processes and discovering of underlying structures and patterns in the data. Designing a message passing mechanism based on multivariate interactions can uncover rich underlying structures in the data, such as clusters and functional modules. We propose a framework that utilizes multivariate interactions for constructing a high-order network and propagating messages within it to uncover the underlying interaction structures in complex data. We present a high-order network construction method using a learning-based approach to identify intricate multivariate interactions from binary interaction information and attribute features. We design a multi-scale message passing paradigm to transmit messages at the node level, edge level and graph level of a high-order network within a unified framework. Finally, we integrate the multi-scale message passing paradigm with a label propagation process to uncover underlying clusters within the data. Experiments conducted on binary network datasets and structured datasets demonstrate that our proposed high-order interactions-based label propagation mechanism outperforms traditional pairwise network algorithms in mining underlying structures.

articleTitle: Class Incremental Learning for Knowledge Acquisition Based on Prototype Network Gating Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: With the development of information technology, the medical field has accumulated a large amount of medical data, which continues to grow. Efficient extraction and effective utilization of knowledge from this vast amount of medical data are crucial for realizing its immense value. Traditional knowledge acquisition algorithms face challenges in effectively identifying and acquiring new types of knowledge in practical applications. To address this, this paper proposes a class-incremental learning method based on a prototype network gating mechanism, called PGMoE. This method integrates multiple experts through a prototype network-based gating mechanism, dynamically adjusting the model's response to new and old knowledge, thereby effectively mitigating the issue of catastrophic forgetting in class-incremental learning. PGMoE not only improves the stability and accuracy of the model in continuous learning processes but also ensures the model's ability to remember historical knowledge. Comparative experiments on multiple datasets with existing class-incremental learning methods demonstrate that PGMoE has significant performance advantages in handling continuous learning tasks.

articleTitle: Adapting Segment Anything Model (SAM) through Prompt-based Learning for Enhanced Protein Identification in Cryo-EM Micrographs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) remains pivotal in structural biology, yet the task of protein particle picking, integral for 3D protein structure construction, is laden with manual inefficiencies. While recent AI tools such as Topaz and crYOLO are advancing the field, they do not fully address the challenges of cryo-EM images, including low contrast, complex shapes, and heterogeneous conformations. This study explored prompt-based learning to adapt the state-of-the-art image segmentation foundation model Segment Anything Model (SAM) for cryo-EM. This focus was driven by the desire to optimize model performance with a small number of labeled data without altering pre-trained parameters, aiming for a balance between adaptability and foundational knowledge retention. Through trials with three prompt-based learning strategies, namely head prompt, prefix prompt, and encoder prompt, we observed enhanced performance and reduced computational requirements compared to the fine-tuning approach. This work not only highlights the potential of prompting SAM in protein identification from cryo-EM micrographs but also suggests its broader promise in biomedical image segmentation and object detection.

articleTitle: Plasma Glucose Reconstruction Based on Data Driven Real-Time Monitoring of CGM Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Real time and accurate monitoring of plasma glucose concentration in diabetes patients is necessary for their condition management. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices can perform plasma glucose monitoring tasks non-invasive by converting the collected interstitial fluid (ISF) plasma glucose into plasma glucose. Reconstructing plasma glucose from ISF has become an important time series prediction problem. Previous research has mainly focused on constructing a chamber model of ISF and plasma for plasma glucose reconstruction. Accurate parameter estimation is the guarantee of the performance of this model driven approach, and this precise parameter estimation is a difficult part of model driving. We propose an end-to-end approach: to complete the plasma glucose reconstruction task in a data-driven manner, obtaining the corresponding plasma glucose sequence at the corresponding time based on the ISF glucose sequence, and the model driven parameter estimation process will no longer be necessary. This end-to-end reconstruction method is one of the advantages of deep learning. This article uses popular time series analysis models in deep learning: LSTM, TCN, Transformer, Informer for plasma glucose reconstruction. Experiments on publicly available datasets have shown the superiority of this data-driven approach over baseline methods.

articleTitle: Knee Osteoarthritis Image Classification Based on A Novel Multi-granularity Feature Fusion Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a prevalent muscu-loskeletal disorder, and the accuracy of its clinical diagnosis often relies on the subjective experience of radiologists. Automated grading of KOA severity with computer assistance holds immense potential as an efficient solution to this challenge. However, previous methods primarily rely on convolutional neural network (CNN) and overlook the limitations of convolutional kernels in extracting global information from knee joint images. Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) effectively improves the global feature extraction performance by transferring and aggregating information through connections between different nodes. In this study, a KOA image classification method based on a novel multi-granularity feature fusion network is proposed by combining CNN and GCN. Firstly, GCN is used to further learn features from different layers of the CNN, aiming to simultaneously capture local and global information from each layer. Then, a spatial attention mechanism is introduced to fuse features of different layers and granularities to effectively alleviate the interference of redundant information. Finally, considering the problem of imbalanced dataset distribution, a specific loss function is introduced to balance the performance of the model on majority and minority classes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other comparable methods with a superior five-class classification accuracy of 0.746.

articleTitle: Hybrid Collaborative Ensemble Clustering for Cancer Gene Expression Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is useful for the analysis of cancer gene expression data. In unsupervised scenario, ensemble clustering uncovers the cluster structure inherent in the gene profiles, which contributes to the advancement of medicine and healthcare research. However, when dealing with cancer gene data, existing ensemble clustering methods have some limitations: 1) the noise features affect the generation of clustering solutions; 2) the integration of clustering solutions ignore the feature subspaces; 3) the unified partition matrix lacks of optimization. In this paper, we propose a hybrid collaborative ensemble clustering framework for cancer gene expression data (HCEC). Firstly, HCEC adopts diverse kernelized PCA schemes to extract compressed feature subspaces and generate multiple clustering solutions, which reduce noise interference and enable the analysis of gene profiles from hybrid perspectives.
