Then, a novel consensus broad learning network is designed that collaborates multiple feature subspaces and cluster structure information to drive a better consensus solution. Through parameter analysis, comparison experiments, and ablation studies, the effectiveness of HCEC has been comprehensively demonstrated on multiple real-world cancer gene expression datasets.

articleTitle: MOADM: Manifold Optimization Adversarial Diffusion Model for Cross-Modality Medical Image Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Diffusion models exhibit excellent diversity in image generation, but the randomness of diffusion models is unnecessary in the process of medical image modality translation. We propose the Manifold Optimization Adversarial Diffusion Model (MOADM) to suppress this randomness and improve the performance of medical image translation. MOADM predicts the linear relationship of evaluation metrics on image manifolds mapped in both latent space and noise space through a manifold consistency predictor. Aiming to select appropriate latent variables and noise, MOADM uses a non-dominated sorting multi-objective optimization genetic algorithm to iteratively optimize images based on the linear relationship, resulting in generated images with better texture, edges, and lower distortion. Extensive evaluations of MOADM against generative adversarial networks(GAN) and diffusion models in multicontrast MRI translation demonstrated superior performance both quantitatively and qualitatively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Single-Source Domain Generalization From CT to MR by Data Augmentation Based on Grayscale Distribution Remapping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: As domain shift hinders deep learning models' performance on medical image analysis, Domain Generalization (DG) has been proposed to enhance the generalization capability. Traditional multi-source domain generalization methods require the training data from multiple source domains, which is often time-consuming and laborious to collect. So, considering that CT and MR are two indispensable medical image domains, we propose a Enhancing Single-Source Domain Generalization from CT to MR by data augmentation based on grayscale distribution remapping to perform tasks of medical image classification and segmentation. First, we put forward Distribution Remapping Module (DRM) to realize effective data augmentation through generating various grayscale distributions based on CT images, thus simulating various grayscale distributions of medical images. Then, each original medical image and its corresponding augmented image form a positive pair. The contrastive loss calculated by these pairs, together with the task loss for medical image classification or segmentation task, is utilized to optimize the model. Compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, experiments on three benchmark datasets, i.e. TotalSegmentator, CHAOS, and AMOS, achieve best performance in both organ classification and segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: ComBat-MLE: A Novel Perspective on Developing and Solving ComBat Harmonization Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: This paper provides a novel perspective on the model development of the ComBat method. Two sets of parameter constraints were introduced to help identify parameters during the parameter estimation process. And Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) was employed to solve the re-formulated ComBat using each set of constraints. The simpler and faster solution was selected as the proposed ComBat-MLE harmonization method. A series of experiments were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of various ComBat variants, both quantitatively and qualitatively. The experiments validated the effectiveness of the proposed ComBat- Mle method in removing non-biological scanner effects while at the same time preserving intrinsic biological information. Although the proposed ComBat-MLE method did not significantly outperform existing ComBat variants, it aids in understanding the ComBat method and offers valuable insights into the development of new harmonization methods.

articleTitle: Predicting Sepsis Onset in ICU Patients Using Machine Learning and Feature Section: A Case Study of MIMIC-IV Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: This study aims to predict the onset of sepsis in ICU patients using multiple machine-learning models with data from the MIMIC-IV database. We employed seven prediction models-Logistic Regression, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Artificial Neural Network, SVM, XGBoost, and Gradient Boosting Decision Tree-using 81 features extracted from routine checks conducted within 12 hours before and 4 hours after ICU admission from 46,530 patients. The features were represented by key values such as maximum, minimum, and mean, referencing the official MIMIC derived daily data tables. XGBoost achieved the best performance with an AUC of 0.81 and an accuracy of 0.729. We then applied Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) to identify the optimal feature subset for each model, finding 13 features commonly selected across all models. This overlap highlights their importance in predicting sepsis and suggests potential for model simplification without losing predictive power. Notably, 6 of these common features overlap with the top 20 SHAP features from the XGBoost model, validating their critical role. Training models with these 18 common features demonstrated that this feature selection process can lead to a simplified, yet effective, predictive model. Thus, we developed a simple, rapid, and practical tool for early detection and clinical intervention of sepsis.

articleTitle: TCMRD-KG: Design and Development of a Rheumatism Knowledge Graph Based on Ancient Chinese Literature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The use of Traditional Chinese medicineTCM in rheumatic diseases dates back to thousands of years ago. Compared with standardized treatment, TCM has the advantages of low cost, low side effects, and flexible medication. Ancient books of traditional Chinese medicine play an important role in clinical and scientific research. This study takes the content related to rheumatism in ancient books of traditional Chinese medicine as the research object, integrates the ontology theory and technology in the knowledge graph, realizes the reconstruction of traditional Chinese medicine information knowledge, and provides basic data structure for data mining and knowledge discovery. This study is the first rheumatism-specific knowledge graph constructed based on ancient books of traditional Chinese medicine; it has tried the construction method of knowledge graph of ancient books of traditional Chinese medicine by combining automatic labeling of mainstream large language models with manual review; and according to the knowledge characteristics of ancient books of traditional Chinese medicine, the existing word segmentation technology is difficult to accurately reproduce the accurate meaning of the original text of ancient books, a new type of entity extraction method is given.

articleTitle: A Mixed Graph Convolutional Network with Cross-Distance Syntactic Aware for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Aspect-based sentiment analysis(ABSA) is one of the text classification tasks, aiming to classify sentiment of aspect words in the given text. Since syntactic information of text can be effectively modeled by dependency tree. Meanwhile, local and global information of sentences can be well learned by graph convolutional network(GCN), so dependency tree-based GCN is widely used in ABSA, where the relationships between sentence words can be effectively captured. However, deep GCN suffers from the problem of over-smoothing, which simply means that nodes of different orders are indistinguishable, especially on small scale datasets. And syntactic information is enhanced early in model training in previous studies. In order to address these problems from other perspectives, first, a mix graph convolutional network with cross-distance syntactic aware for ABSA is proposed, to alleviate nodes over-smoothing of GCN problem. Second, Mixhop is combined with GCN, to help the aspectual node to acquire feature information of multi-layer neighbors. The proposed model, not only allows aspect words to fuse the information learned from the shallow-layer neighbors, but also fuses the information from deep-layer neighbors. Third, attention mechanism is used to focus on syntactic information of nodes that are distant from the aspect words. Finally, experiments conducted on widely used public datasets that the proposed model achieves superior results.

articleTitle: Computational analysis and modeling of Gut Microbe Data: ASD Identification and Potential Biomarkers Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Background: As research on the gut-brain axis continues to intensify, there is growing evidence of a potential link between the gut microbe (GM) and autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Gut microbes have great potential as physiological indicators for ASD recognition. Methods: This study combined microbiome analysis, machine learning modeling, and animal experiments to explore the roles of GM in ASD recognition. We built a XGBoost-based ASD identifier on 16S rRNA data of human, and combined machine learning and statistical analysis to select potential GM markers. Furthermore, we studied the offspring of maternally immune-activated mice to analyze the differences in early life GM and behavior between Poly(I:C)-treated and PBS-treated mice by examining the mice's GM and related behaviors. Results: The experimental results showed significant differences between GM of ASD patients and healthy individuals, with low diversity and richness in the overall environment. The machine learning-based identifier achieved a good performance with an ASD recognition rate of 91.9% along with an MCC value of 0.599. Selection results for potential GM markers contained five genus-level microbes: Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium, Roseburia, Faecalibacterium, and Paraprevotella. The results of animal experiments showed that the mice did not exhibit obvious behavioral abnormalities early in life, but the richness and diversity of their gut microbiota were significantly reduced, suggesting that the gut microbiota had been altered before the mice developed autism symptoms. Taken together, this study can provide clues for exploring the mechanism of the influence of GM on ASD, and will help early identification and clinical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Recurrence Risk Prediction for Differentiated Thyroid Cancer Using Local Clustering Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Thyroid cancer incidence in women has risen sharply in China from 2000 to 2016. Differentiated thyroid cancer has a relatively low mortality rate but a higher recurrence rate. The American Thyroid Association (ATA) risk model, based on traditional clinical and pathological parameters, may not fully capture all factors affecting recurrence risk. Deep learning technology has shown potential in predicting recurrence in patients with well-differentiated thyroid cancer, but its application to heterogeneous tabular medical data remains challenging. We propose a local clustering contrastive learning method to address the challenges of applying deep learning to tabular medical data. This method divides features into random subsets, performs clustering within each subset, generates positive and negative sample pairs, and trains encoders and a decoder to maximize the InfoNCE output. The learned feature representation is used for downstream classification tasks. The proposed method was applied to a retrospective cohort of 383 patients diagnosed with thyroid cancer at a medical center. Experimental verification on this dataset and ten public tabular datasets demonstrated the effectiveness of the method in risk-stratifying patients with well-differentiated thyroid cancer. The proposed local clustering contrastive learning method effectively leverages the complexity of tabular medical data, enhancing the learned feature representation and enabling accurate recurrence risk prediction for well-differentiated thyroid cancer. This approach can assist doctors in making personalized treatment decisions, such as the necessity, dosage, and frequency of radioactive iodine treatment, ultimately improving patient care.

articleTitle: Ensemble Causal Structure Learning for Data with Mixed Feature Relationships: Application to Lung Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In the medical field, lung cancer is a major public health problem. Nowadays, most studies on lung cancer mainly focus on correlation analysis, while there are few studies mining the causal relationships of risk factors for lung cancer. Existing causal structure learning methods require that the data satisfy certain assumptions, that the relationship between features is a single linear or nonlinear relationship, and that the distribution of features is only a single Gaussian or non-Gaussian case. The assumption leads to the inability of causal structure learning methods to mine their causal relationships in real-world lung cancer datasets. To address the above problems, we propose the Ensemble Causal Structure Learning for data with Mixed Feature Relationships (ECSL-MFR). The method ensembles different types of causal structure learning methods through the proposed causal intensity intensity aggregation operator. The method is generally applicable and can be applied to complex healthcare settings. The experiment has demonstrated the powerful competitiveness of our method, particularly in SHD, where the best effect of our method can be reduced by 78% compared to the baseline method. Furthermore, our method can identify causal relationships in actual lung cancer data.

articleTitle: Learning Rate Optimization for Medical Image Classification Based on Federated Learning and Gaussian Process Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Image classification is always a very important research topic in the medical field. The current medical image classification is mainly based on artificial intelligence methods. The main problem of existing methods is the slow speed, precision of training, and redundant iteration. To solve this problem, Li et al. proposed Gaussian process regression-based learning rate optimization (GLRO) method. This method solves the problem of redundant iteration and improves classification accuracy. Gaussian process regression is used to improve the optimization effect of the optimizer and further improve the classification accuracy. However, the limitation of this method is that it uses a single training network and loss function. To improve this medtod, we propose a more efficient federated learning method called FedGPM. We train on many classification networks with loss functions more appropriate to the properties of medical images. The results show that our algorithm improves on the original GLRO algorithm and has a very good performance. The accuracy rate on the NIH chest X-ray dataset is 95% to 97%, and the accuracy rate on the specific dataset is close to 99%.

articleTitle: Pre-Training and Fine-Tuning Transformer for Brain Network Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) is a widely used diagnostic tool for brain psychiatric disorders, providing valuable data for artificial intelligence applications in brain science. However, the scarcity of labeled data presents a significant challenge for medical diagnostics since the acquisition of labeled medical data is both time-consuming and costly. The lack of data often leads to over-fitting problem and therefore decreases the brain network classification ability. To address this problem, we propose a Pre-Training Transformer model for brain network classification, which includes the pre-training phase and fine-tuning phase. In the pre-training stage, the unlabeled brain network is randomly masked and then the encoder extracts features from the masked brain network while the prediction head reconstructs the masked regions of the brain network using these features. In the fine-tuning stage, the classification model comprises the pre-trained encoder from the previous phase and a classification head based on labeled dataset. By using pre-training technique, the model are able to learn generalized characterization and distribution of data to improve performance on subsequent downstream tasks. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, we conduct comparative experiments on ABIDE I, ABIDE II, and ADHD-200 datasets, respectively. Experiment results on two commonly used brain atlases (AAL90 Atlas and CC200 Atlas) show that our proposed method not only achieves better performance in fully utilizing unlabeled data but also alleviates the over-fitting problem.

articleTitle: Joint Explicit and Implicit Cross-Modal Interaction Network for Anterior Chamber Inflammation Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Uveitis demands the precise diagnosis of anterior chamber inflammation (ACI) for optimal treatment. Current diagnostic methods only rely on single-modal data, which leads to poor performance. This may be attributed to the current lack of publicly available multi-modal datasets and the lack of a fusion method for the task of diagnosis for ACI. Specifically, existing fusion methods focus on empowering implicit interactions (i.e., self-attention and its variants) but neglect explicit cross-modal interactions, especially clinical knowledge and imaging properties, which are crucial to the diagnosis task. To this end, we propose a joint Explicit and implicit Cross-Modal Interaction Network (EiCI-Net), which uses anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) images, slit-lamp images, and clinical indicators (tabular data) as input. In detail, we develop CNN-Based Encoders and a Tabular Processing Module (TPM) to extract feature representations of different modalities. Next, we devise an Explicit Cross-Modal Interaction Module (ECIM) to generate attention maps as a kind of explicit clinical knowledge based on the tabular feature maps, then integrate them into the slit-lamp feature maps, allowing the model to focus on more effective informativeness of the slit-lamp images. After that, the Implicit Cross-Modal Interaction Module (ICIM), a transformer-based network, implicitly enhances modality interactions. Finally, we construct a considerable real-world multimodal dataset, which will be made available publicly, and conduct extensive experiments to evaluate the superior performance of EiCI-Net compared with other methods. In addition, the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of explicit cross-modal interaction, which has always been ignored before.

articleTitle: DKGC-LSTM:Fusion of Domain Knowledge to Guide CNN and LSTM for Heart Failure Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In the medical field, integrating domain-specific knowledge into disease risk prediction has become increasingly important. Despite significant advancements in deep learning techniques for handling time-series electronic health records (EHR) data, current methods often overlook the integration of domain knowledge with patient data. This paper proposes a novel method, DKGC-LSTM, for heart failure prediction based on time-series EHRs. The proposed approach utilizes domain-knowledge-guided Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM).The method consists of two main components: First, LSTM is employed to process the detection values of heart failure patient features. To address irregular time intervals in EHR data, positional encoding is incorporated into the LSTM units. Second, associations between heart failure features and the disease are extracted from a medical knowledge graph. These associations are combined with laboratory test values to form feature-disease triples, which are then processed using a CNN model to extract high-dimensional features representing the relationships between the disease and the features.Finally, these two components are integrated to construct a cascading prediction model. Experiments on the MIMIC-IV heart failure dataset demonstrate that, compared to traditional methods, this model significantly enhances prediction accuracy and recall when handling continuous data.

articleTitle: Smart Microscope for Online Detection of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: A common goal of microscopy is to assist experts in analyzing the sample status and tailoring research strategies by observing and collecting specific images. Utilizing microscopy to examine the pathological lesions of tissue slices for Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) and provide treatment plans is a common practice among pathologists. Recently, pre-trained artificial intelligence (AI) models have been applied to assist pathological whole slide images (WSIs) detection. However, most analysis methods rely on digital WSIs from a scanner. This dependence limits the sensitivity of models due to image style differences and increases imaging and computational costs. To address these defects, we propose a smart microscope for executing online HCC detection. By integrating a fine-tuned vision-language model (VLM), the framework achieves real-time imaging and detection for morphological correlations of liver tissues under the lens. We fine-tuned the VLM by 365 collected WSIs containing HCC and evaluated the proposed method on 87 clinically hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained histological slides. The experiments demonstrated that our microscope achieved 100% sensitivity during online detection, which consistency is in pair with pathologists. Meanwhile, the high-confidence HCC fields are recorded precisely. The proposed framework aims for pathologists to improve diagnostic efficiency.

articleTitle: Interpretable Disease Prediction Based on Kolmogorov - Arnold Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: The application of machine learning in the medical field has been a burgeoning area of research over the past decade. However, a significant challenge lies in the interpretability of disease prediction models. This study proposes a novel disease prediction model based on Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN), aiming to provide a new approach to an interpretable model architecture. KAN is a novel neural network architecture that extends the network derived from the Kolmogorov-Arnold rep-resentation theorem, enhancing the transparency and reliability of the model by constructing an interpretable network structure. This paper first introduces the theoretical foundation of KAN and its network design principles. It then validates the model's effectiveness in various disease prediction tasks through a comprehen-sive series of experiments and conducts a comparative analysis with existing machine learning models. The experimental results demonstrate improvements in various performance metrics, such as accuracy, average precision, aera under ROC, area under PR curve, compared to traditional models. Importantly, KAN enhances the model's transparency, enabling medical experts to comprehend the logic behind the predictions. This interpretability is crucial for clinical decision-making, as it allows healthcare professionals to understand the reasoning behind the model's outputs and make informed decisions based on the provided insights. The experimental codes can be downloaded from: https://github.com/keyan2017/KAN4Medicine.

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: DCP++: A New Registration Method for Brain MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In geometric computer vision, 3D registration is a critical task for various applications. 3D medical image registration, as one important application of 3D registration, holds substantial clinical potentials for supporting diagnosis, surgeries, and treatments through the registration of images captured at different times or using different modalities. Recently, the rapid advancement and widespread adoption of deep learning have spurred interest in applying this technology to the registration of point cloud data. In this paper, an deep-learning-based 3D brain MRI medical data registration algorithm (DCP++) is constructed. Through employing reasonable loss function, DCP++ achieves efficient and precise registration of 3D brain data. To evaluate the performance of DCP++, we apply the algorithm to the point cloud registration task of 3D human brain MRI images from the ADNI public dataset. Benchmark comparisons, ablation experiment, and visualization analyses are conducted. Experiments demonstrate that compared with state-of-the-art algorithms, DCP++ reduces the registration error by approximately 90%. Tests on real data confirm the accuracy and robustness of the DCP++ algorithm, highlighting its potential in medical practice.

articleTitle: A Lung Nodule Labelling and Recognition Method Based on Variational Auto Encoder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally, and early diagnosis significantly improves the 5-year survival rate to over 60 % when the tumor is small and asymptomatic. With the continuous development of artificial intelligence, deep learning has gradually become a prominent topic. However, current lung nodule detection models have several disadvantages, including a large number of parameters, which hinder practical deployment, and poor interpretability of the generated results. To address these issues, the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) can be applied to lung nodule detection. This approach helps reduce the number of model parameters, improve deployability, and enhance the interpretability of the results. However, VAE also has limitations, primarily in the following aspects: it is less effective than mainstream models in generating lung nodule labels and cannot directly generate such labels. In this study, we combine VAE, self-supervised learning, and concept extraction to construct a lung nodule detection model with fewer parameters, improved generation performance, and better interpretability. Our goal is to use the model to distinguish latent spaces in CT images related to lung nodules. We then integrate self-supervised learning to enhance the representation of different concepts, ultimately to generate labeled images of lung nodules using an additional mask decoder. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art lung nodule detection algorithms on the LUNA16 and LNDB datasets. Furthermore, we provide interpretable descriptions of the generated results on the LUNA16 dataset. The code for the main structure of the model has been committed to github: https://github.com/sunshine-bov888/vae-lungnode.

articleTitle: Emotional EEG Recognition and Classification Based on GCN Combined with LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Emotion recognition technology is becoming more and more widely used in the medical field, and it plays an important role in the evaluation and monitoring of mental health by accurately capturing the emotional state of individuals. This technology allows doctors to have a deeper understanding of how patients are feeling in order to provide customized treatment. In addition, the combination of emotion recognition technology with medical devices, such as smart wearable devices, can monitor patients' mood changes in real time, providing doctors with key data to make more precise medical decisions. This research delves into deep learning-based emotion recognition techniques, especially for EEG applications. The study used the DEAP dataset, which recorded the electrophysiological brain responses of 32 healthy adults while watching 40 music videos. The data was collected at a frequency of 512Hz and covered 32 EEG channels to capture mood changes comprehensively. Subjects were subjectively assessed on a four-dimension emotional scale (Valence, Arousal, Dominance, Liking). In this study, the graph convolutional neural network (GCN) was used to integrate the spatial features of EEG and the signals in the time domain or frequency domain to conduct a comprehensive analysis of emotion. Considering the temporal characteristics of EEG signals, the study also incorporates long short-term memory network (LSTM) for emotion analysis. In this paper, innovation is carried out in feature extraction and model construction. The correlation between spatial features and channels is fully utilized in feature extraction stage, and the combination method of GCN and LSTM is adopted in model construction. By combining frequency domain and spatial features and applying graph convolutional neural network, this study achieves a high accuracy of 93.21%, demonstrating the accuracy of emotion recognition technology.

articleTitle: FoTNet: An Effective Deep Learning Model for Preoperative Differentiation of Common Malignant Brain Tumors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: s Glioblastoma(GBM), primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL), and brain metastases (BM) are three common malignant central nervous system tumors. Currently, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is commonly utilized in clinical settings to aid neurosurgeons in preoperative diagnosis. Due to the similar anatomical structures and imaging characteristics, it's quite difficult to distinguish these three tumors, even for experienced clinicians. In practice, preoperative non-invasive differentiation is imperative as the treatment modalities and prognosis are significantly different for these tumors. This study aims to use deep learning models to perform a three-class classification of brain T1-weighted MRI images for GBM, BM, and PCNSL cases, verifying if it offers satisfactory performance as a reference for clinicians' preoperative diagnosis. We create a new multi-center brain MRI imaging dataset. Our dataset includes 315 training cases (GBM 64, PCNSL 59, BM 192) and 124 external test cases (24:23:77). We utilize these contrast-enhanced T1-weighted (T1-CE) MRI images for the training and testing of our CNN model tailored to this tumor classification. We design a novel and effective CNN framework, termed as FoTNet. It encompasses various architectural designs tailored specifically for this task, such as patichify operation and deeper networks to extract local fine-grained features. FoTNet especially integrate a frequency-based channel attention layer within the network and adopt focal loss to mitigate performance issues stemming from imbalanced training data. Our model exhibits outstanding classification performance on the test set, achieving a tumor imaging classification accuracy rate of 92.50%, with an average AUC of 0.9754. The model's classification capability significantly surpasses previous studies using machine learning or deep learning techniques for the imaging classification of these three types of tumors. Through our research, we develop a convolutional neural network with excellent performance in tumor classification tasks. Our findings suggest that this AI-based model might be a valuable resource to assist physicians in differentiating between GBM, PCNSL, and BM, especially in resource-limited settings, aiding in the preoperative diagnosis of brain tumors.

articleTitle: KEMedGPT: Intelligent Medical pre-consultation with Knowledge-Enhanced Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Large language models(LLMs) are driving productivity advancements in the fields of medical healthcare and information systems. Existing medical LLMs types vary widely and frequently pose challenges for small and medium-sized enterprises(SMEs) to deploy. To address these limitations, we propose KEMedGPT: a knowledge-enhanced medical GPT specifically designed to improve the medical knowledge and consultation capabilities of LLMs. KEMedGPT employs a two-stage strategy and leverages the unique medical text Q&A data from an Internet medical society for training. This approach simulates human-like decision-making processes using real-world patient data, enhancing the model's relevance and applicability. Our experiments demonstrate that KEMedGPT excels in multi-turn dialogue for pre-consultation, effectively facilitating interactive exchanges that enhance the early identification of patient needs and the delivery of personalized medical advice. This capability significantly improves medication safety and elevates the overall quality of healthcare services. Extensive and rigorous evaluations of the model highlight KEMedGPT's superiority, outperforming existing general and specialized large language models.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Breast Cancer Segmentation on Small Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Breast cancer, a disease with a relatively high incidence, is typically diagnosed by histopathological analysis of microscopic images. However, this manual process suffers from low efficiency and high expertise requirements. Deep learning-based image segmentation offers the potential to automate the identification and delineation of breast cancer lesion areas in histopathological images, thereby improving diagnostic efficiency and lowering the expertise threshold. Existing deep learning models for this task typically require large annotated datasets, posing practical limitations. This paper proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN) based model that can learn effective feature representations from smaller datasets. The model adopts an encoder-decoder architecture, drawing on the deep-shallow feature fusion strategy of DeepLabv3+. By incorporating a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and a double-layer convolution-based feature fusion module, the proposed model improves feature extraction capabilities with limited data and mitigates overfitting. Evaluation of the proposed model on the CAMELYON16 dataset demonstrates its ability to extract discriminative features and accurately segment breast cancer lesion areas, even with a relatively small training set. These results highlight the potential of the approach to address the data scarcity challenge in histopathology-based breast cancer diagnosis, paving the way for more accessible and efficient computer-aided diagnosis systems.

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: Multi-scale Histopathology Image Registration based on Radiation-Variation Insensitive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In clinical diagnosis, multimodal medical imaging technology is crucial for accurately assessing patients' conditions. This article addresses the registration issues of histopathological images, particularly Whole Slide Images (WSI), proposing a multiscale registration method based on radiation-variation insensitive features. Differences in light absorption, reflection, and transmission due to various tissue staining and imaging devices result in radiation distortions between images. Traditional preprocessing techniques such as grayscale conversion and normalization can partially mitigate color differences but fail to completely eliminate variations in brightness and contrast. This study introduces the improved Radiation-Variation Insensitive Feature Transform (RIFT) for WSI registration, combining Features from Accelerated Segment Test (FAST) keypoint extraction, RIFT descriptor computation, Fast Sample Consensus (FSC) keypoint filtering, and affine transformation registration using ADMM-based multiscale iterative optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that this algorithm effectively addresses “radiation distortions” in WSI and is suitable for registering high-resolution and large-angle image pairs. Validation using the ANHIR dataset shows excellent performance in terms of average, median, maximum registration errors, and robustness.

articleTitle: Spectral Clustering Enhanced Classifier Chain Ensemble for Multi-Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: In the clinical diagnosis scenario, most patients suffer from multiple diseases simultaneously. Multi-disease prediction models can effectively predict the risk of patients suffering from multiple diseases based on electronic health record (EHR) data, which has become a typical multi-label classification (MLC) problem in the field of machine learning. However, there are few multi-disease prediction models that can address the problem of imbalanced class distribution in the data. Additionally, most existing MLC algorithms focus solely on solving the data imbalance problem without considering label correlations. To solve the aforementioned problems, this paper proposes an enhanced classifier chain ensemble (SC-ECCE) algorithm based on spectral clustering for multi-disease prediction. The dynamic sample-specific oversampling algorithm (DSSO) is proposed to mitigate the negative impact of imbalanced class distribution. In order to verify the effectiveness and superiority of the SC-ECCE algorithm, experiments are conducted on ten multi-label datasets from different fields and a real-world multi-label medical dataset, NHANES(2017-2018). The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SC-ECCE algorithm outperforms the MLC baselines in three evaluation indicators.

articleTitle: Parallel Computing-Based Genome-Wide Epistasis Analysis of CSF Total Tau in ADNI Cohort
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Epistatic interactions, often overlooked in traditional genome-wide association studies (GWAS), are increasingly recognized as crucial for elucidating the “missing heritability” in Alzheimer's disease (AD). To comprehensively investigate the role of epistasis in AD, we conducted a parallel computing-based genome-wide epistasis analysis focusing on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) total tau (T-tau), a key AD biomarker, in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort. Leveraging the computational efficiency of GPUs, we employed a multiple linear regression model adjusted for diagnosis, age, and gender, and identified 1,273 statistically significant SNP-SNP interaction pairs. While these pairs exhibited marginal main effects individually, they collectively explained a substantial portion of T-tau variance, highlighting the importance of considering epistasis when investigating the genetic basis of quantitative traits (QT) CSF T-tau. Furthermore, we identified 19 interacting gene pairs within established protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks and confirmed the involvement of 358 previously reported AD-related genes. Notably, we identified nine specific epistatic interactions potentially implicated in AD pathogenesis, synaptic function, and cognitive decline, representing promising candidates for future mechanistic studies and therapeutic development. Our study demonstrates the power of parallel computing-based genomewide epistasis analysis in uncovering complex genetic interactions and their contribution to AD.

articleTitle: T-M Net: A Fusion Convolutional Neural Network Method for Lung Aging Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: As the population ages, the precise assessment of pulmonary senescence becomes essential for the diagnosis and management of chronic respiratory diseases. However, existing medical imaging analysis techniques encounter significant chal-lenges due to data scarcity, especially in the domain of lung CT imaging. This research proposes an innovative method for assessing lung aging in CT images-T-M Net. This method combines transfer learning and MS-CNN to improve the accuracy and efficiency of lung aging assessment in CT images. We employed a pretrained ResNet18 model, capitalizing on transfer learning to harness the insights from extensive datasets, thereby minimizing the computational demands of model training. Furthermore, a channel attention mechanism is integrated within the transfer learning framework to heighten the model's focus on critical pulmonary regions, thus augmenting its predictive accuracy and interpretability. To accommodate the distinctive characteristics of lung CTs, a MS CNN architecture was developed, capturing multi-dimensional information ranging from microscopic details to macroscopic structures through variously sized convolutional kernels. Testing on a lung CT dataset revealed that our approach surpasses traditional methods in accuracy and generalizability, underscoring its potential utility in the early diagnosis and effective treatment of pulmonary ailments.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Weighted Broad Network for Imbalanced Medical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Medical diagnosis is crucial for providing quality healthcare. Machine learning techniques have received much attention in the medical field for their ability to provide efficient handling of diverse diagnostic problems. Nonetheless, machine learning often faces performance degradation due to imbalanced data in medical diagnosis, and also requires models that can quickly diagnose problems to facilitate doctors' medical decisions. To address this problem, we introduce Adaptive Fuzzy Weighted Broad Learning System (AFWBLS), which aims to use a variety of technologies to improve medical diagnostic accuracy. The adaptive weight enables BLS to take Intra-class density, inter-class density, the distribution of classes and frontier into consideration, which can reduce the impact of imbalanced data. The fuzzy weight gives BLS the ability to reduce the impact of noise and outliers. The Experiment shows that AFWBLS has good performance on imbalanced medical datasets and AFWBLS can maintain stable in datasets with large imbalanced rates.

articleTitle: Review on Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Health
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) encompasses a wide array of technologies that emulate human intelligence to perform tasks such as diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient management in healthcare. Recent innovations in AI, such as deep learning, natural language processing, and robotics, have significantly transformed medical practices. This review highlights key innovations, including AI's role in enhancing diagnostic accuracy through imaging analysis, optimizing treatment strategies with predictive analytics, and improving patient outcomes via personalized medicine. By focusing on both virtual and physical branches of AI in healthcare, this paper underscores the transformative impact of AI, aiming to bridge gaps in efficiency, precision, and patient care.

articleTitle: Machine Learning to Predict Surgery Duration: Towards Implementing AI and Digital Twin for Effective Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Traditional elective patients' surgical scheduling relies on plan-makers' subjective estimates or historical averages, leading to inefficiencies such as surgery cancellations or underutilisation of resources. Machine learning (M/L)-based predictive algorithms offer a promising solution with data-driven models to forecast surgical times, however, their application in NHS hospital settings remains limited. This study explores the implementation of multiple M/L algorithms for surgical time estimation for Trauma and Orthopaedics related procedures in an NHS Trust hospital. Results indicate that Neural Networks, along with ElasticNet regression, Gradient Boosting, and Bayesian Ridge regression models, demonstrate robust performance. Additionally, expansion to procedure specific models, built separately for each procedure shows promising results. This study contributes insights into the integration of M/L algorithms into healthcare digital resources, paving the way for enhanced surgical planning strategies. Future research will focus on integrating the predictive models into a comprehensive AI driven Digital Twin framework for simulation and optimisation-driven automated decision-making.

articleTitle: Predicting Complications of Cirrhosis using Synthetic Data Generation Enhanced Dynamic Classifier Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Early identification of the risk of complications in cirrhosis is essential for facilitating timely interventions, personalized treatment plans and better patient management. However, developing data-driven models using real-world Electronic Health Records (EHRs) data is often hindered by challenges related to data accessibility, integrity, sparsity and class imbalance. Synthetic data that captures the characteristics and patterns of real-world EHRs data can be used for model development and evaluation that effectively addresses these data-related issues. In this study, we propose a dynamic classifier selection-based framework that incorporates both real-world EHRs data and synthetic data generated by generative adversarial networks. The framework trains a diverse set of heterogeneous classifiers, leveraging the benefits of both data sources. By utilizing dynamic classifier selection, the framework adaptively selects the best classifier based on the specific characteristics of the input data. The proposed framework was assessed through experiments to evaluate its effectiveness in the early prediction of the prevalence of acute on chronic liver failure and hepatic encephalopathy. The experimental results consistently demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework compared to baseline approaches. This study showcases the potential of the framework to improve clinical predictions and contribute to advancing our understanding of disease progression.

articleTitle: Emotional Interaction Activities for Home Robots based on EEG Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: This study presents an emotion detection system utilizing Electroencephalogram (EEG) data, integrated into the home robot's human-robot interaction model. With advancements in affective computing technology, the demand for home robots has been on the rise, offering emotional support and companionship through emotion recognition and responses, significantly enhancing the user experience. Leveraging the DEAP dataset, this study achieved real-time recognition of users' emotional states through preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification model training. We downsampled, removed artifacts from, and filtered the raw EEG signals, extracting features from the frequency, time, spatial domains, and brain networks. LASSO regression was employed for feature selection, followed by the application of various machine learning algorithms for emotion classification. The experimental results showed that the KNN classifier performed best in emotion recognition, achieving an average accuracy of 90.3%. Further human-robot interaction tests validated the system's practical applicability, with participants rating highly the precision of emotion detection, the timeliness of interactive responses, and the overall experience. The proposed EEG-based emotion recognition system shows significant potential in enhancing the human-robot interaction experience for home robots, while also suggesting directions for further improvements in real-time performance and personalized models.

articleTitle: DAC-UNet: Dual Attention CNN-Enhanced CswinUnet for Gastric Cancer Pathological Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Gastric cancer is one of the most lethal cancers. Currently, clinical diagnosis primarily relies on gastroscopic biopsies and the manual experience of doctors to assess the development of lesions in tissue sections. However, pathological screening requires a significant amount of time from specialized pathologists. Due to variations in clinical experience and limitations in medical resources, the detection of gastric cancer still faces challenges. Traditional methods for segmenting gastric cancer images often overlook the hierarchical structure of features and the spatial details, both local and global, in the lesion images. To address the above issues, this paper proposes a hybrid and efficient pathological image segmentation network named DAC-UNet, designed for precise pathological image segmentation tasks. DAC-UNet uses Cswin Transformer blocks to build a hierarchical structure, allowing it to capture global information with less computational complexity. The network also includes multi-scale dual attention skip connections between the encoder and decoder to preserve local spatial details and improve global interactions across different scales. We conducted a thorough theoretical analysis of this method and validated it on a gastric slice dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves outstanding performance on both our gastric slice dataset and the MoNuSeg dataset. Specifically, on our gastric slice dataset, we obtained a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 89.42% and an HD95 of 47.24, while on the MoNuSeg dataset, we achieved a DSC of 79.28% and a 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 19.38.

articleTitle: Multi-View Feature Fusion Encoding and Memory-driven Report Generation for OCTA Fundus Image Diagnosis*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Medical Artificial Intelligence (MedAI)
abstract: Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography (OCTA) has recently emerged as a novel, non-invasive, and rapid angiographic technology. However, several challenges including small lesion areas, limited effective information, noise interference, and blurred lesion boundaries in OCTA fundus images complicate automatic image interpretation. Traditional image caption models struggle with lesion detection and are inadequate for generating comprehensive, multi-sentence reports. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a multi-view feature fusion encoding and memory-driven report generation model. This model effectively combines shallow spatial structural information with deep feature information to achieve a detailed visual representation of lesion characteristics. Utilizing a relational memory module, it queries and enhances textual features, thereby improving the generalization ability of the report generation model. A new dataset of OCTA retinal image reports was constructed, and comparative experiments with state-of-the-art report generation methods were conducted on this dataset, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.
